summary: Describes using the Generic Associated Channel Label in pseudowires in MPLS Transport Profile networks. It updates RFC 5586 by removing a restriction on using that label for pseudowires. It is a standards-track document.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC removes a restriction on using the Generic Associated Channel Label with pseudowires in MPLS-TP. It makes the stated use consistent across MPLS and MPLS-TP environments.

questions: can gal be used with pseudowires
what does rfc 6423 change in rfc 5586
subtitle: Allows the Generic Associated Channel Label to be used with MPLS-TP pseudowires.

tldr.problem: RFC 5586 prohibited using the Generic Associated Channel Label with pseudowires in MPLS-TP, while placing no such restriction on other MPLS environments.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 6423 updates RFC 5586 so the label may be used with pseudowires in MPLS-TP as well as other listed MPLS structures.
tldr.outcome: The GAL can be used with LSPs, concatenated LSP segments, Sections and pseudowires in both MPLS and MPLS-TP.

today: RFC 6423 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 5586. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates RFC 6423.

sections.title: The Associated Channel and GAL
sections.content:
RFC 5586 generalizes the Associated Channel mechanism for Sections, Label Switched Paths (LSPs) and pseudowires (PWs) in MPLS networks. It defines the Generic Associated Channel (G-ACh) and a Generic Associated Channel Label (GAL) that works with the Associated Channel Header (ACH).

RFC 5586 allowed GAL use with pseudowires in other MPLS environments but prohibited it with pseudowires in MPLS-TP.
sections.plainLanguage: The GAL works with an associated channel header on MPLS network structures. An earlier rule treated pseudowires differently in MPLS-TP than in other MPLS environments.

sections.title: Removing the Pseudowire Restriction
sections.content: The RFC says the different treatment of pseudowires could lead to unnecessary differences between implementations and conflicts with the MPLS-TP requirements in RFC 5654. RFC 6423 specifies that the GAL can be used with packets on a G-ACh on LSPs, concatenated segments of LSPs, Sections and PWs in both MPLS and MPLS-TP.
sections.plainLanguage: The update allows the same listed GAL uses in both types of MPLS environment. This removes the earlier ban on using it with MPLS-TP pseudowires.

sections.title: Updated Text and Security
sections.content:
The update adds pseudowires to the Introduction's description of where the GAL works with the ACH. In Section 4.2, RFC 5586's MUST NOT use GAL with PWs becomes MAY use GAL with PWs for MPLS-TP.

The updated text says the presence of a GAL indicates that an ACH immediately follows the MPLS label stack. The security section says there are no additional security considerations beyond those in RFC 5586.
sections.plainLanguage: The earlier prohibition becomes permission. The updated text also says that an ACH follows the label stack when a GAL is present.
